label: prf:pieri-photon-shift
title: Proof of pieri photon shift
html:
Proof. Write the degree-one element as \gamma = 1 + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \phi_i \, \sigma_i with scalar coefficients \phi_i (degree-one volume lemma), and let \beta_m be supported purely on the \lambda-block. Here the support \mathrm{supp}(x) of an element is the set of labels in the Young lattice indexing the isotypic components on which x has a non-zero component, read through Schur–Weyl duality: at generic q, the Hecke algebra H_n(q) and \mathrm{SU}_q(2) generate each other's commutant on V_\square^{\otimes n}, where V_\square is the two-dimensional fundamental representation, and the simple module V_\lambda is matched with the \lambda-isotypic component of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) action [kassel1995]. The hypothesis on \beta_m says its image lies in the V_\lambda-isotypic component.

Support convention. The element \gamma \beta_m is of mixed degree: the identity term of \gamma leaves \beta_m at level n of the tower, while each generator term couples one further strand and lands at level n + 1. Support is therefore tracked in the Wedderburn labels of the tower algebra \bigoplus_m H_m(q), one label set per level. At level n + 1 we write \lambda + \square := (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2) \vdash n+1 and \lambda - \square := (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) \vdash n+1; the name of the latter comes from the two-row \mathrm{SU}_q(2) identification, under which a complete two-box column carries the trivial determinant weight and (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) column-reduces to (\lambda_1 - 1, \lambda_2). All partitions in a given support statement below live at the level indicated.

Step 1: reduction by linearity. Since \gamma \beta_m = \beta_m + \sum_i \phi_i \, (\sigma_i \beta_m) and \mathrm{supp}(x + y) \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(x) \cup \mathrm{supp}(y), it suffices to bound the support of each summand. The identity term contributes the level-n component \mathrm{supp}(\beta_m) = \{\lambda\}, unchanged. It remains to show, at level n+1, \mathrm{supp}(\sigma_i \beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda + \square\} \cup \{\lambda - \square\} for each generator term.

Step 2: a single crossing couples one fundamental factor. Each generator term couples the degree-one strand to the state through exactly one crossing \sigma_i. In the Schur–Weyl picture the coupled object lives in

  V_\lambda \otimes V_\square,

the isotypic component of the state tensored with the fundamental representation carried by the coupled strand. The crossing acts by the braiding, which is a morphism of \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-modules (the Hecke action commutes with the quantum-group action), so it preserves the isotypic decomposition of V_\lambda \otimes V_\square: the support after coupling is contained in the set of \mu for which V_\mu appears in V_\lambda \otimes V_\square.

Step 3: the Pieri rule. The quantum Clebsch–Gordan rule for \mathrm{SU}_q(2) at generic q — the one-box case of the Pieri rule — decomposes

  V_\lambda \otimes V_\square
  \;\cong\;
  \bigoplus_{\mu = \lambda \pm \square} V_\mu,

with multiplicity one for each summand ([fulton1997], Ch. 2; [kassel1995], Ch. VII). The two summands are the two level-(n+1) blocks \lambda + \square = (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2) and \lambda - \square = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) of the support convention (when (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) is a valid two-row shape; otherwise only \lambda + \square occurs, and the containment below holds a fortiori). Hence \mathrm{supp}(\sigma_i \beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda + \square\} \cup \{\lambda - \square\} at level n+1.

Step 4: assembly. Combining Steps 1–3,

  \mathrm{supp}\bigl(\gamma \cdot \beta_m\bigr)
  \;\subseteq\;
  \{\lambda\} \;\cup\; \{\lambda + \square\} \;\cup\; \{\lambda - \square\},

which is the claimed containment. \blacksquare

Scope. The proposition gives a containment of supports, not equality. The actual coefficients are dictated by the \phi_i and the Hecke-algebra 6j-symbols (matrix elements of the basis change between the seminormal basis and the inclusion basis); we do not compute them here. For the purposes of the QOU mass-formula pipeline, only the support statement is used: it bounds the spectral spread induced by a single photon coupling to one box.

Relation to the volume vanishing. The degree-one volume lemma says \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\gamma) = 0. The Pieri shift is the representation-theoretic counterpart: it tracks how \gamma moves the Wedderburn support without itself contributing to the archimedean volume of \overline{\gamma}.
